title: Practice Pack: Force and Laws of Motion
subject: Science
chapter: Topic-based: use with whichever Class 9 book your students follow
instructions: Level 1 checks the ideas, Level 2 is board-style numericals, and Level 3 is Foundation-level challenge.
Key relations: p = mv · F = ma = (change in momentum)/time · momentum before = momentum after (when no external force acts).
Convert g → kg and km/h → m/s before you substitute.

questions.q: State Newton's first law of motion.
questions.answer: An object stays at rest, or in uniform motion in a straight line, unless an unbalanced external force acts on it.

questions.q: Why do passengers lurch forward when a moving bus stops suddenly?
questions.answer: Because of inertia of motion. The bus stops, but the passengers' bodies tend to keep moving forward.

questions.q: Define momentum and give its SI unit.
questions.answer: Momentum is the product of mass and velocity (p = mv). Its SI unit is kg m/s.

questions.q: A rubber ball and a stone are the same size. Which has more inertia, and why?
questions.answer: The stone, because it has more mass. Inertia depends on mass.

questions.q: State Newton's third law of motion with one example.
questions.answer: To every action there is an equal and opposite reaction, and the two act on different bodies. Example: a gun recoils backwards when a bullet is fired forwards.

questions.q: A force of 5 N gives mass m_{1} an acceleration of 10 m/s^{2} and mass m_{2} an acceleration of 20 m/s^{2}. What acceleration would it give if both masses were tied together?
A car of mass 1200 kg moving at 90 km/h is slowed down to 18 km/h in 4 s. Find the acceleration, the change in momentum, and the force applied.
questions.answer: u = 25 m/s, v = 5 m/s. a = (5 – 25)/4 = –5 m/s^{2}. Change in momentum = 1200 × (5 – 25) = –24,000 kg m/s. Force = ma = 1200 × 5 = 6000 N (opposite to the motion).

questions.q: An object of mass 100 kg is accelerated uniformly from 5 m/s to 8 m/s in 6 s. Find its initial and final momentum and the force applied.
A bullet of mass 20 g is fired from a pistol of mass 2 kg with a velocity of 150 m/s. Find the recoil velocity of the pistol.
questions.answer: Total momentum before = 0. So 0.02 × 150 + 2 × v = 0, which gives v = –1.5 m/s. The pistol recoils at 1.5 m/s, opposite to the bullet.

questions.q: A hockey ball of mass 200 g moving at 10 m/s is hit so that it goes back along its path at 5 m/s. Find the change in its momentum.
questions.answer: Take the initial direction as +. Change in momentum = m(v – u) = 0.2 × (–5 – 10) = –3 kg m/s. The magnitude is 3 kg m/s, opposite to the original direction.

questions.q: Two objects of masses 100 g and 200 g move along the same line and direction at 2 m/s and 1 m/s respectively. They collide, and after the collision the first object moves at 1.67 m/s. Find the velocity of the second object.
questions.answer: Momentum before = 0.1 × 2 + 0.2 × 1 = 0.4 kg m/s. After: 0.1 × 1.67 + 0.2 × v = 0.4, so 0.2v = 0.233 and v ≈ 1.165 m/s (same direction).

questions.q: Why does a cricketer pull the hands backwards while catching a fast ball? Use the idea of force and time.
questions.answer: The ball's momentum has to be reduced to zero. Moving the hands back increases the time taken to stop the ball. Since F = (change in momentum)/time, a longer time means a smaller force on the hands, so they hurt less.

questions.q: A truck starts from rest and rolls down a slope with constant acceleration, covering 400 m in 20 s. Find its acceleration and the force acting on it if its mass is 7 tonnes.

closing: Momentum questions: always choose a positive direction first!
